svg.text: Lower-body evaluation — loading-gate tests
Hip · knee · ankle — ranges, control and symmetry · 2 sessions (~50 + ~20 min)
Muscle group
Hip / glutes
Knee (quads, hamstrings)
Ankle / calf
Before you start — what this is, and how the phone is used
What: tests that decide when each lower-body joint may move up one loading stage. Order: A, B, C, then D.
When: a rested day, no lower-body training or badminton the day before. Warm up 5 min (walk or bike).
Day after: no badminton — the symmetry tests take calves, quads and glutes to technical failure.
Phone = camera only: on the tripod ~2 m away, level, lens at the height the card names; never in your hand.
Beat: a metronome on a second device (PC, tablet or speaker), loud enough for the video to record it.
iPhone (iOS 18 or later): turn on Settings → Camera → Record Sound → Allow Audio Playback.

a.text: Angles: later, on the PC, in Kinovea (free): open the video, pause on the frame, pick the card's tool,

svg.text: drag its centre onto the joint, note the number (over 180°: 360 minus it), snip the frame (Win+Shift+S).
Pictures move when this file opens in Edge or Chrome; elsewhere they show the start (dark) and end (faint).
Kit: the 20 cm box · bench · wall · frame or rack to hold · mat · tape measure · tape · tripod and phone
a second device for the beat · Kinovea on the PC · barefoot for every test
A — Session 1: Ranges (~15 min · no weights · your own effort only; card 5 leans body weight)
Hip bend range, knee bent — each leg
Set-up
Lie on your back on the mat, legs straight, side-on to the
camera, 2 m away, lens at floor level, the tested leg
nearest the camera.
Do
Bring the knee toward your chest as far as it goes by
itself: hip muscles only, no hands; the knee bends freely,
the other leg stays flat. Hold 2 s; lower. 3 tries per leg.
Read
Kinovea, end frame: Angle tool, centre on the hip, one leg
along the mat toward your feet, the other to the knee.
Write down
The best of 3, per leg. Training limit: 70–80% of it (squat
and hip-thrust depth).
3 tries per leg
Mat · tripod · phone
Straight-leg raise range — each leg
Set-up
As card 1: on your back, legs straight, the tested leg
nearest the camera, lens at floor level.
Do
Raise the straight leg as far as it goes by itself, the
other leg flat on the mat; don't force the knee straight.
Hold 2 s; lower. 3 tries per leg.
Read
Kinovea, top frame: Angle tool, centre on the hip, one leg
along the mat toward your feet, the other to the ankle.
Write down
The best of 3, per leg. RDL depth stops at 70–80% of it.
3 tries per leg
Mat · tripod · phone
Hip side-lift range, standing — each leg
Set-up
Stand facing the camera, 2 m away, lens at hip height, one
hand on the frame, feet together, belt line level.
Do
Lift the straight leg out to the side as far as it goes by
itself, toes forward, pelvis and trunk still. Hold 2 s;
lower. A try whose belt line tilts doesn't count. 3 tries
per leg.
Read
Kinovea, top frame: Angle-to-vertical tool along the lifted
leg, hip to ankle.
Write down
The best of 3, per leg. Training limit: 70–80% of it (hip
machine, banded hip work).
3 tries per leg
Frame · tripod · phone
Knee range — each leg
Set-up
Lie on your back, legs straight, side-on, lens at floor
level, the tested leg nearest the camera.
Do
Tighten the thigh to straighten the knee fully; hold 2 s.
Then slide the heel along the mat toward your buttock as far
as it goes by itself; hold 2 s. 3 tries per leg.
Read
Kinovea, both end frames: Angle tool, centre on the knee,
legs to the hip and the ankle.
Write down
Both numbers per leg, and whether the heel lifts off the mat
as you straighten (= the knee bows past straight: yes/no).
3 tries per leg
Mat · tripod · phone
Knee-to-wall lunge (ankle range) — each leg
Set-up
Barefoot, face the wall, tested foot pointing straight at
it, toes ~10 cm away, the other foot a step behind, hands on
the wall. Lens side-on at shin height, tested leg nearest
the camera.
Do
Bend the front knee slowly to touch the wall, heel flat,
knee over the second toe; hold 2 s. If it touches, move the
foot back 1 cm and repeat; stop at the last touch with the
heel down. No bounce.
Read
Kinovea, the last clean touch: Angle-to-vertical tool along
the shin, ankle to knee.
Write down
That angle and the toe-to-wall gap (cm), per leg. Training
limit: 70–80% of the angle.
1 cm steps, per leg
Wall · tape measure · tripod
B — Session 1: Control tests (~15 min · each clean or not · film every one)
Step-down — each leg
Set-up
Barefoot on the 20 cm box, tested foot near its edge, the
other leg hanging beside it, hands on hips. Camera in front,
2 m, lens at knee height. Metronome 60: 2 beats down, 2 up.
Do
Bend the standing knee slowly until the other heel just
touches the floor, no weight on it, then straighten, knee
soft at the top. 10 reps per leg.
Fail if
On any rep the knee drifts inside the second toe (valgus) or
the pelvis drops on the free side; any pain.
Write down
Clean or not, per leg.
10 reps per leg
20 cm box · tripod
Heel-raise control set — each leg
Set-up
Barefoot on one leg on a flat floor, fingertips on the wall
at shoulder height, knee straight but soft. Camera behind
you, 2 m, lens at ankle height. Metronome 60: up on one
beat, down on the next.
Do
Rise onto the ball of the foot as high as it goes, then
lower to the floor. 10 reps per leg, on the beat.
Fail if
A rep stops short of your first reps' height, the heel
wobbles in or out, a beat is missed, or any pain.
Write down
Clean or not, per leg. Then card 8.

a.text: Video: Missy Fraser PhD, single-leg heel raise ↗

svg.text: 10 reps per leg
Wall · tripod
Single-leg stance, 30 s — each leg
Set-up
Barefoot on one leg, arms crossed on the chest, eyes open,
the other foot just off the floor beside the ankle. Camera
in front, lens at ankle height.
Do
Hold 30 s per leg.
Fail if
The lifted foot touches down, the standing foot wobbles or
shifts, the arms uncross, or any pain.
Write down
Clean or not, per leg. Cards 7 and 8 together are the
ankle's control test: both clean.
30 s per leg
Tripod · phone
Single-leg squat — each leg
Set-up
Barefoot on one leg, arms crossed on the chest, the other
leg held a little forward. Camera in front, 2 m, lens at hip
height. Metronome 60: 1 beat down, 1 up.
Do
Squat until the knee is bent about 60° (two-thirds of a
right angle, thigh well above parallel), then stand. 5 reps
per leg, on the beat.
Fail if
Any of Crossley's five is not good: overall (balance,
smooth, on the beat), trunk (leans or turns), pelvis (drops
or turns), hip (thigh drifts in), knee (moves inside the
foot); any pain.
Write down
Good or not, per criterion, per leg.

a.text: Video: USC Athletic Training, single-leg squat ↗

svg.text: 5 reps per leg
Tripod · phone
C — Session 1: Symmetry tests (~20 min · each leg to technical failure · ≥3 min between sides)
Single-leg sit-to-stand — each leg
Set-up
Seat: the low box on the bench, thighs just above parallel
when seated. Sit on its front half, foot on a tape mark, the
other leg held forward off the floor, arms crossed. Lens
side-on at seat height. Metronome 60: 2 beats down, 2 up.
Do
Stand up on one leg, knee soft at the top; lower for 2 beats
to touch the seat without sitting; stand again. Keep going.
Stop when
A rep misses the beat, the free foot touches down, the arms
uncross, the trunk lurches or rocks to get up, the knee
caves in or snaps straight, or the seat takes your weight.
Write down
Reps before the first miss, per leg; seat height in cm.

a.text: Video: Physiotherapy UC Copenhagen, one-leg sit to stand ↗

svg.text: 1 set per leg
Bench · low box · tripod
Single-leg bridge — each leg
Set-up
On your back on the mat, the tested heel on the bench, knee
bent ~20°, the other leg held straight up, arms crossed on
the chest; mark the heel spot. Lens side-on at bench height.
Metronome 60: up on one beat, down on the next.
Do
Push the heel down to lift the hips until shoulder, hip and
knee line up; lower to a light touch on the mat. Keep going.
Stop when
The hips miss the top line, a beat is missed, the heel
slides, the pelvis twists, or you rest at the bottom.
Write down
Reps before the first miss, per leg.

a.text: Video: Sport Rehab Guide, single-leg hamstring bridge ↗

svg.text: 1 set per leg
Bench · mat · tripod
Single-leg heel raises — each leg
Set-up
As card 7: barefoot, flat floor, fingertips on the wall at
shoulder height, same spot every time. Lens side-on at ankle
height. Metronome 60: up on one beat, down on the next.
Do
Heel raises as high as they go, knee straight but soft; keep
going, on the beat.
Stop when
A rep misses full height (against your first reps), misses
the beat, the knee bends, or you lean on the wall.
Write down
Reps before the first miss, per leg.

a.text: Video: Missy Fraser PhD, single-leg heel raise ↗

svg.text: 1 set per leg
Wall · tripod
D — Session 2: 2–7 days later (~20 min · symmetry tests only)
Repeat 10–12 — other side first
Set-up
2–7 days after session 1: the same warm-up, seat, heel spot,
wall spot, beat and set-up. Start with the other side.
Do
Tests 10, 11 and 12 once more.
Score
Mean of both sessions, weaker ÷ stronger: ≥90% passes.
Example
Heel raises left 27 and 28, right 30 and 30: 27.5 ÷ 30 =
92%, a pass.
1 set per leg
As session 1
Step-gate log — after every training session (exit criterion 1)
Per joint: pain ≤5/10 during and after · back to normal the next morning · no swelling or warmth
within 24 h · no “loose joint” feeling that day.
Two clean weeks in a row are needed; a fail is a flare and restarts the count.
Every test — rules
These are tests, not training sets: follow each card's set-up exactly
Stop at pain, a clunk, or a slipping or giving-way feeling — that test is not clean this round
Same seat, box, spots, set-up and beat every time; barefoot; write down the seat height
Film every test and judge it on the paused video, not by feel
Ranges: your own effort only, nothing pushes further — except card 5's slow lean, heel flat
No stretching before the range tests
What the results unlock — the same tests at every stage step
A joint moves up one loading stage when all three hold: 2 clean step-gate weeks, a clean control test
and a symmetry score of ≥90% over both sessions. Passing now opens stage 2 only.
Knee at stage 2: squats may go below parallel, within 70–80% of your card-4 bend (R1 · R3).
For 2→3: train ≥2 clean weeks at stage 2, then run this file again; the same for 3→4.
The ranges (A) set your training limits at every stage; redo them after a flare.
A flare drops a joint back one stage · court work (cardio routine) needs ankle, knee and hip at stage 4.
Rules behind this file: Stage 0 §2.5–2.6 · R1 · R3 · R14 · D-61 · D-62 · D-67…D-69 · D-77…D-82 (gymspec).
Send back to Claude — results per joint
Hip: bend ° L/R · leg-raise ° L/R · side-lift ° L/R · test 9 per criterion L/R · bridge reps L/R ×2
Knee: straight and bent ° L/R · heel lifts? L/R · test 6 clean? L/R · sit-to-stand reps L/R ×2 · seat cm
Ankle: shin ° and gap cm L/R · tests 7–8 clean? L/R · heel-raise reps L/R ×2
All: the Kinovea snips · step-gate clean weeks so far, per joint
